transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 40 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Daniel Wu (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Pinelake CTO), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Harpreet Singh (Security), Nina Park (Product)

Summary: quick renewal check and alignment on EU private on‑prem pilot + capacity bump. Discussed latency SLOs, KMS/HSM expectations, pricing delta for dedicated vs private, and pilot benchmarks.
Topics: renewal timing, EU on‑prem pathway, capacity uplift (dedicated vs burst), security artifacts, benchmark plan.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick agenda — renewal timeline, eu on‑prem pilot plan, and a short benchmark next steps.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: yeah great thanks, we are on a tight timeline, quarter end renewal and we need eu data residency plus lower lat to our eu customers.
[00:30] Evan Brooks: cool, can you remind us current usage footprint? tokens per month, p95 lat etc — helps us size the dedicated pool or on‑prem nodes.
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: sure, rough numbers — 120M tokens/month right now, peak concurrency around 40 rps, typical p95 at 220ms when hitting hosted, but we see spikes to 450ms during peak with small model variants.
[01:05] Daniel Wu: got it. so two levers: dedicated capacity in eu region or private on‑prem. dedicated gives predictable throughput, private gives residency+control but cost delta.
[01:25] Sofia: exactly. our legal/security folks are pushing for on‑prem or VPC with customer‑managed keys.
[01:33] Harpreet Singh: hi — from security high level we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and retention controls. also proof of soc2 and some standard pen test artifacts.
[01:49] Maya: yes we can provide SOC2 report and the security packet — i'll share the secure link after the call.
[01:59] Harpreet: when you say KMS, do you support bring‑your‑own‑key? like integrated with our cloud KMS or HSM appliances?
[02:10] Evan: short answer yes — we support BYOK for both dedicated and private deployments; for on‑prem we can integrate with customer HSMs over pkcs11 or cloud KMS. there was a small note in the docs about network firewall rules that i will resend.
[02:30] Nina Park: from product perspective we care about model parity — are we getting the same model variants in eu private as hosted? sometimes replicas have quant differences.
[02:42] Daniel: good question. our onboarding ensures model parity — the runtime picks kernels per hw. in private we usually ship a vetted quant profile; there can be minor token perf differences but we test for output fidelity.
[03:05] Liam: on cost, ballpark delta vs hosted? our finance wants a simple number: if we move 50% of traffic to eu private what's the uplift?
[03:18] Maya: ballpark — private on‑prem carries infra + ops and licensing; for the mid‑sized footprint you're describing it's typically 1.6x to 2x the hosted unit cost, but we can scope a dedicated gpu pool which is often cheaper than full on‑prem. i'll put exact scenarios in the pricing doc.
[03:40] Sofia: timeline — we need a pilot before Oct 15 to decide for renewal. can we do a two‑week benchmark run?
[03:50] Evan: yes we can schedule a benchmark in your staging eu cluster. we'll test throughput, p95/p99, and model quality regression against your golden prompts.
[04:05] Harpreet: also want to validate that audit logs include per‑request metadata and token counts for billing reconciliation.
[04:16] Daniel: logs include request id, model version, token counts, latencies; for privacy we can disable payload logging and still capture metadata.
[04:30] [TAP] (background noise)
[04:35] Maya: quick note — competitors came up in your RFP, GoliathAI and CloudServe were mentioned?
[04:42] Sofia: yeah we ran a bake‑off earlier and GoliathAI had a cheaper per token for the small model but no private on‑prem option. CloudServe had on‑prem but performance was inconsistent.
[04:58] Ethan (customer voice mis‑attributed): um — i think the other vendor had pretty slow kv cash performance, sorry cache — kv cache.
[05:10] Evan: haha — kv cache, yes. our continuous batching and prefix caching usually helps p95 lat's without sacrificing cost too much.
[05:22] Liam: question on scaling — if we want to burst to 100 rps during campaigns, what's the recommended approach?
[05:30] Daniel: recommended path is a hybrid — dedicated base capacity sized for steady state + burst capacity (hosted) or autoscaling fleet in private with a buffer. that gives predictable costs and headroom.
[05:48] Nina: for canary and rollouts, do you support pinning model versions and automatic fallback? we want safe deployments.
[05:58] Evan: yes we do canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. we also surface token‑level cost in the console.
[06:12] Sofia: good. one red flag for ops is boot time for private nodes — how long till a node ready for traffic?
[06:22] Daniel: on‑prem boot depends on infra — with our prebuilt image it's usually 8–12 minutes for the runtime to register, GPU warmup is another few mins. dedicated cloud pools are faster but still have provisioning window.
[06:40] Liam: fine. for the benchmark we need specifics: model sizes to test, sequence length, and a throughput target.
[06:48] Evan: we'll propose tests: 1) base model (7B) at 256 seq for standard NLL, 2) larger 13B with 512 seq for chat, and 3) embedding workload. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and tail.
[07:05] Sofia: sounds good. please include error rates and mem/cpu/gpu utilization.
[07:13] Evan: will do.
[07:18] Harpreet: on encryption at rest, we need FIPS compliant modules in the chain for some customers — can you confirm?
[07:26] Daniel: for private deployments we can enable FIPS‑mode crypto stacks and integrate with your HSM. for dedicated hosted we rely on cloud provider FIPS modules — we'll share details.
[07:40] Maya: action items recap coming at the end. quick question — renewal length, are you looking 12 or 24 months?
[07:49] Sofia: 12 months with an option to extend after pilot; we prefer shorter initial to validate on‑prem.
[07:56] Maya: ok we'll price both and show the delta.
[08:02] [Timestamp jump]
[20:17] Liam: jumping ahead — about billing, can you export token level billing to our billing system via S3 or push to a partner connector?
[20:27] Daniel: yes we can export detailed billing reports hourly to an S3 bucket or push to your billing pipeline.
[20:34] Harpreet: do logs include user PII by default? we need to be sure payloads are not stored.
[20:41] Evan: payload logging is off by default for private; for hosted we annotate but you can opt out — we'll show config.
[20:50] Nina: product question — if we opt for private on‑prem, how do we get model updates?
[20:57] Daniel: we ship model artifacts via an authenticated artifact repo and support staged upgrades; you control when to apply. for critical security patches we recommend a tighter window.
[21:12] Sofia: ok great. next steps on scheduling: Evan, you said you can run a bench week of 9/14?
[21:20] Evan: yes our ops will spin up tests on 9/14, it'll take roughly 3 days to complete a full slate.
[21:27] Maya: i'll send the pricing scenarios by 9/10 and share the SOC2 + security packet link.
[21:35] Harpreet: i'll send the security questionnaire to Maya and Evan by 9/11.
[21:40] Maya: perfect. any other open points?
[21:46] Sofia: one last — can you provide an SLA for p95? we need p95 under 200ms for the european region as a contract objective.
[21:55] Daniel: we can commit to a best‑effort p95 under 200ms for dedicated pools with the right sizing and caching; for private on‑prem it's dependent on your infra but we'll work to meet that SLO in the pilot and include fallback policies.
[22:12] Liam: will you add a fallback model variant in the plan so we don't drop requests if capacity hits?
[22:18] Evan: yes automatic fallback to a cheaper variant is in the rollout playbook.
[22:25] [Crosstalk: agreement and wrap]
[22:30] Maya: ok thanks all — recap of next steps in the chat, i'll follow up with docs and the pricing PDF. meeting adjourned.

End of recording.
